correctness.rationale: The Gram kernel equals a periodic mean-zero weighted zeta tail F_max; Abel summation gives O(m^-2), and an explicit two-triangle nuclear decomposition makes the difference S1. Finite trace identity proves the conditionally convergent harmonic trace. A Hilbert–Schmidt discretization of the Hardy kernel and logarithmic Fourier Weyl sequences prove σess(C*C)=[0,4], hence the positive essential spectral interval and norm. Sang’s explicit translation criterion supplies the Toeplitz dichotomy. Finite checks were executed and do not replace proof.

value.rationale: A natural noncompact operator family that is generally excluded from the Toeplitz algebra nevertheless has its modulus in the commutator ideal. A trace-class (rather than merely compact) cancellation yields the exact essential singular spectrum for every period and a computable arithmetic trace defect; unit-modulus alternating phases provide the strongest exact-modulus separation. This quantitatively resolves a motivated modulus-versus-membership question rather than an arbitrary finite special case.
